q: How is the position of a metal in the reactivity series related to the ease of obtaining it from its ore?
options: The lower the metal in the series, the easier it is to obtain
The higher the metal in the series, the easier it is to obtain
All metals are equally easy to obtain
Only metals above carbon can be obtained
explain: Unreactive metals lose their compounds easily, while reactive metals hold on to oxygen strongly and need more energy-intensive methods.

q: Which metal is found uncombined in the Earth's crust?
explain: Gold is very unreactive, so it exists as the element, while the others occur as compounds.

q: Which ore is used to extract iron in the blast furnace?
explain: Hematite contains iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃, and bauxite is the aluminium ore.

q: Which set of materials is added to the blast furnace?
options: Bauxite, coke, limestone and hot air
Hematite, cryolite, limestone and hot air
Hematite, coke, limestone and hot air
explain: The furnace uses iron ore, coke as fuel and reducing agent, limestone to remove impurities and hot air for oxygen.

q: Which row correctly gives the role of a substance in the blast furnace?
options: Coke | burns to give heat and carbon dioxide
Limestone | reduces iron(III) oxide to iron
Hot air | forms slag with impurities
explain: Coke burns in the hot air to release heat and form carbon dioxide, which is then reduced to carbon monoxide.

q: What is the role of limestone in the blast furnace?
options: It burns to provide heat for the furnace
It decomposes to form calcium oxide, which removes acidic impurities as slag
It reduces iron(III) oxide to iron
It provides the oxygen needed to burn coke
explain: Limestone breaks down into calcium oxide, which reacts with silicon dioxide impurity to form slag.

q: Which compound forms the slag in the blast furnace?
explain: Calcium oxide from the limestone reacts with silicon dioxide to form calcium silicate.

q: Which substance acts as the reducing agent for iron(III) oxide in the blast furnace?
explain: Carbon monoxide removes oxygen from iron(III) oxide and is oxidised to carbon dioxide.

q: What happens to iron(III) oxide in the blast furnace?
options: It gains oxygen and is oxidised
It loses oxygen and is reduced to iron
It is neutralised by carbon monoxide
explain: Reduction here means the removal of oxygen from the oxide to leave the metal.

q: Which equation shows iron(III) oxide being reduced by carbon monoxide?
explain: Two iron atoms and three oxygen atoms need three CO to take the oxygen, giving 2Fe and 3CO₂ in a balanced equation.

q: Which equation shows carbon dioxide being reduced to carbon monoxide in the blast furnace?
explain: Carbon dioxide reacts with hot carbon to form carbon monoxide, with carbon dioxide losing an oxygen atom.

q: Which equation shows the formation of slag in the blast furnace?
explain: Basic calcium oxide reacts with acidic silicon dioxide to make calcium silicate.

q: Molten slag floats on molten iron in the blast furnace. Why?
options: Slag has a higher density than iron
Slag is solid at the furnace temperature
Slag has a lower melting point than the hot air
Slag has a lower density than iron
explain: The less dense slag forms a layer on top, so the two liquids can be run off separately.

q: What is the purpose of the hot air blown into the base of the blast furnace?
options: It provides oxygen for the coke to burn
explain: Oxygen in the air burns the coke, releasing the heat needed and producing carbon dioxide.

q: Which row correctly gives an ore and extraction method?
options: Aluminium | hematite | reduction with carbon monoxide
explain: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite by electrolysis, and iron from hematite by reduction in the blast furnace.

q: Why can aluminium not be extracted from its oxide by heating with carbon?
options: Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Aluminium oxide has a low melting point
Aluminium oxide does not contain oxygen
explain: Carbon cannot remove oxygen from the oxide of a metal more reactive than itself.

q: What is the role of cryolite in the extraction of aluminium?
options: It raises the melting point of the mixture
It is the ore from which aluminium is obtained
It lowers the melting point of aluminium oxide
It reduces aluminium oxide to aluminium
explain: Aluminium oxide melts at a very high temperature, and dissolving it in molten cryolite reduces the temperature and energy needed.

q: Why do the carbon anodes in aluminium extraction need to be replaced regularly?
options: They react with oxygen to form carbon dioxide and burn away
They dissolve in the molten cryolite
They are reduced by the aluminium
They are coated with aluminium and stop working
explain: Oxygen formed at the hot anode reacts with the carbon, which is gradually used up.

q: Which half-equation shows the reaction at the cathode in the electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide?
explain: Positive aluminium ions go to the negative cathode and gain electrons (reduction) to form aluminium.

q: Which half-equation shows the reaction at the anode in the electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide?
explain: Oxide ions lose electrons at the positive anode (oxidation) to form oxygen gas.

q: Which row correctly describes the cell used to extract aluminium?
options: Carbon | aluminium oxide in molten cryolite | cathode
Carbon | aluminium oxide in molten cryolite | anode
Copper | aluminium oxide in molten cryolite | cathode
explain: Carbon electrodes are used with aluminium oxide dissolved in molten cryolite, and aluminium forms at the negative cathode.

q: What mass of iron can be obtained from 320 g of iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃, in the blast furnace? (Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16)
explain: Mr of Fe₂O₃ = 160, so 320 g is 2.0 mol, which gives 4.0 mol of Fe and so 4.0 × 56 = 224 g.

q: What mass of aluminium can be obtained from 204 g of aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃? (Ar: Al = 27, O = 16)
explain: Mr of Al₂O₃ = 102, so 204 g is 2.0 mol, which gives 4.0 mol of Al and so 4.0 × 27 = 108 g.

q: Which metal can be extracted from its oxide by heating with carbon?
explain: Carbon can reduce only oxides of metals below it in the series, which includes zinc.

q: A metal is more reactive than carbon. How is it usually extracted from its ore?
options: By heating the ore with carbon
By heating the ore on its own
By filtering the ore with water
By electrolysis of the molten compound
explain: Carbon cannot reduce the oxides of metals above it in the series, so electrolysis is used.

q: Which equation represents copper(II) oxide being reduced by carbon?
explain: Two CuO supply two oxygen atoms, which react with one carbon to form CO₂, giving a balanced equation.

q: Which substance is not added to the blast furnace?
explain: Cryolite is used in the extraction of aluminium, not iron.

q: Which equation shows carbon (coke) burning completely in air to provide heat in the blast furnace?
explain: The first step is the combustion of carbon in oxygen from the air, an exothermic reaction.

q: Which sequence correctly describes how the reducing agent forms and acts in the blast furnace?
options: Coke burns to CO₂, CO₂ reacts with more coke to give CO, and CO reduces Fe₂O₃
Coke burns to CO, CO reacts with Fe₂O₃ to give CO₂, and CO₂ reduces coke
CaCO₃ gives CO, CO reacts with coke, and coke reduces Fe₂O₃
Fe₂O₃ gives CO₂, CO₂ reacts with coke, and CO reduces Fe₂O₃
explain: Carbon dioxide from burning coke is reduced by more coke to CO, and the CO then reduces the iron(III) oxide.

q: Which gas is formed when iron(III) oxide is reduced by carbon monoxide?
explain: Carbon monoxide takes oxygen from the oxide and is oxidised to carbon dioxide.
